headline: Blood and Betting: Inside Meridian's Dojo Underground Circuit
body:
For fourteen months, this reporter embedded with sources inside the Dojo Underground — a network of illegal augmented-combat arenas operating across seventeen confirmed sites beneath The Narrows, Geartown, and the flooded service tunnels of Old Harbor. What we found is an industry generating an estimated 40 million quanta annually, with fighters competing in three tiers: unaugmented, chrome-assisted, and the prohibited Apex class, where participants run military-grade Arcturus Defense combat rigs stripped of their limiters. Fighters range from desperate the Gray Zone residents to off-contract runners burning through savings. Promoters take forty percent of all bets.

The operation is not disorganized. Seven of the seventeen venues are owned outright by Iron Lotus shell companies registered under false Palladian business licenses. Fixed matches, enforcement squads, and a medical blacksite operated by a disgraced Helix Biosystems physician — identified in documents seen by this publication as Dr. Tomás Ekwueme-Sato — keep the circuit running with brutal efficiency. 'I came in needing 6,000 quanta for my daughter's NovaMind rejection surgery,' said one fighter, speaking under the alias Crow. 'Three months later I still owe them 9,000. You don't leave the circuit. The circuit leaves you.'

Meridian Municipal Enforcement confirms it has opened an investigation but declined to say whether any venues have been identified. Sources within the Graycloaks allege that three MME precinct commanders in The Narrows receive monthly payments from Dojo Underground operators, which would explain why a network this large has operated without a single public arrest in over four years. Arcturus Defense denied that any of its hardware appears in the underground circuit and called the claim 'categorically false and legally actionable.'
aftermath: The Lake Monitor exposé triggered a high-profile MME raid on five venues within two weeks, but twelve sites had already relocated; Dr. Ekwueme-Sato disappeared before investigators reached the medical blacksite, and Iron Lotus restructured the circuit under new shell identities within ninety days.
runner_relevance: The exposé created a volatile two-sided contract market almost overnight. Iron Lotus hired extraction specialists to relocate fighters and equipment before MME raids hit, paying premium rates for speed — some extractions cleared 7,000 quanta in under six hours. Simultaneously, Graycloaks offered data-retrieval contracts for the financial records tying the shell companies to Iron Lotus accounts, and the Lake Monitor itself contracted runners for source protection and secure courier work throughout the investigation. Post-raid, several displaced fighters began hiring themselves out as enforcement runners, creating a new class of cheap, combat-capable contractors flooding The Narrows job boards.
